periods.analysis: Harborview entered the cycle with communicable disease controlled at 35 per 100k, comfortably below the <=45 target, which tells us routine surveillance, vaccination access, and school reporting are doing their job. The Emergency Response Readiness Score was 86 against a >=90 target, so the quarter is appropriately yellow: not unsafe, but not yet at the reliability standard I want for a fast-growing coastal city of 165,000. The gap was concentrated in after-hours call-down completion and cache reconciliation at the North Pier medical reserve site, where two pediatric airway bins and several PPE pallets required manual verification. This is a prevention issue as much as an emergency issue; readiness has to be built before the storm, the spill, or the outbreak arrives.
periods.recommendations: Keep the green disease-rate performance by sustaining weekly syndromic surveillance reviews with Harborview General, the three urgent-care groups on Route 7, and school nurse leads. Close the readiness gap by running a focused call-down drill for Health Department, Fire EMS, and Community Emergency Response Team leads, with a documented target of 90% confirmation within 45 minutes. Complete barcode tagging and expiration checks for the North Pier cache before the next quarterly inventory, and report exceptions by asset bin rather than in aggregate.

periods.analysis: In 2024-Q4, the communicable disease case rate rose from 35 to 43.2 per 100k, still green and still below the <=45 target, but close enough to the threshold that we should not be casual about winter respiratory season. The Emergency Response Readiness Score held flat at 86, remaining yellow against the >=90 target and showing that the Q3 weaknesses were not yet fully corrected. The increase in disease activity was consistent with influenza-like illness reported from the Seabreeze High and East Harbor clinic clusters, not a single uncontrolled outbreak. Operationally, the city remained stable, but stable at 86 is not the same as ready at 90.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the respiratory prevention push through pop-up vaccine hours at the Ferry Terminal, Seabreeze High, and the Bayside senior buildings, with same-week outreach to cohorts showing lower uptake. Require the Logistics Section to finish North Pier cache reconciliation and produce a variance list for PPE, antivirals, and pediatric supplies. Repeat the after-hours call-down in January and track nonresponse by role so we know whether the issue is staffing, contact data, or procedure.

periods.analysis: By 2025-Q1, the communicable disease case rate improved from 43.2 to 39.9 per 100k, keeping us green below the <=45 target after the winter peak. The Emergency Response Readiness Score increased from 86 to 88, a useful move in the right direction but still yellow because the standard is >=90. The improvement followed the January call-down refresh and partial completion of cache barcoding, especially for the Harborview Annex and North Pier locations. I read this as evidence that the system responds when we give teams clear tasks, but we are still two points short of the level needed for dependable surge activation.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the decline in communicable disease by continuing rapid school absenteeism review every Monday and Thursday through the end of respiratory season. Move readiness from 88 toward 90 by completing the remaining medical reserve barcode work and testing the updated contact roster with a no-notice evening drill. Add pharmacy and long-term-care liaisons to the drill, because those partners are often the first to see supply and staffing stress.

periods.analysis: In 2025-Q2, the communicable disease case rate dropped again from 39.9 to 33.9 per 100k, a strong green result and the best prevention signal since this review began. The Emergency Response Readiness Score improved from 88 to 89, still yellow but now one point from the >=90 target. The spring tabletop with Fire Station 4, Harborview General, and the Port Authority clarified shelter medical staffing, but the exercise after-action report still listed backup generator fuel documentation at the Civic Center shelter as incomplete. This quarter shows momentum: disease burden is down, and the readiness program is nearly across the line, but nearly is not our public-health standard.
periods.recommendations: Preserve the green disease trend by extending wastewater and urgent-care signal review into summer travel season rather than pausing after respiratory season. Close the final readiness point by documenting Civic Center generator fuel contracts, testing satellite phones at North Pier and City Hall, and assigning an owner for each open after-action item. Schedule a functional exercise, not another tabletop, for Q3 so the score reflects practiced operations.

periods.analysis: In 2025-Q3, the communicable disease case rate edged down from 33.9 to 33.5 per 100k, remaining green and showing that summer travel and waterfront events did not translate into broad community transmission. The Emergency Response Readiness Score slipped from 89 to 88, keeping the objective yellow and reminding us that readiness can decay quickly when staff rotate and supplies expire. The slippage was tied to delayed onboarding for two new epidemiology duty officers and expired N95 fit-test records for several shelter medical volunteers assigned to the Marina District cooling-center plan. The population-health picture is healthy, but the operational bench still needs discipline.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the low case rate by keeping event-based surveillance for the Harborview Seafood Festival, cruise-shuttle route, and marina clinics through the end of September. Recover the readiness score by completing duty-officer onboarding within 30 days and clearing all expired fit tests before the next volunteer deployment roster is approved. Institute a monthly readiness huddle with epidemiology, EMS, emergency management, and logistics so small lapses are corrected before they become score losses.

periods.analysis: In 2025-Q4, the communicable disease case rate rose from 33.5 to 41.7 per 100k, still green under the <=45 target but again reflecting predictable winter pressure. The Emergency Response Readiness Score fell from 88 to 86, returning to the level we saw at the start of the arc and keeping the quarter yellow. The disease increase was driven by respiratory and gastrointestinal reports from school, childcare, and two assisted-living cohorts, with no evidence of citywide uncontrolled spread. The readiness decline is the more important management signal: supply-chain substitution for isolation gowns and incomplete volunteer credential renewals slowed the annual shelter activation drill.
periods.recommendations: Protect the green case-rate result by intensifying vaccination, hand-hygiene, and stay-home-when-sick messaging in childcare centers, assisted-living facilities, and winter recreation programs. Stabilize readiness by approving alternate gown vendors, pre-clearing volunteer credentials 60 days before expiration, and requiring Logistics to run a mid-quarter inventory of all shelter medical totes. I also want a corrective-action tracker reviewed biweekly until the Emergency Response Readiness Score is back above 88.

periods.analysis: In 2026-Q1, the communicable disease case rate improved from 41.7 to 38.1 per 100k, keeping Harborview green and moving away from the <=45 threshold after winter. The Emergency Response Readiness Score rose from 86 to 88, a meaningful recovery but still yellow against the >=90 target. The improvement followed credential catch-up clinics for Medical Reserve Corps volunteers and the addition of a secondary gown supplier through the regional purchasing cooperative. We are back on the upward path, but the lesson from 2025 is clear: readiness has to be maintained as a routine clinical habit, not repaired after each drill.
periods.recommendations: Continue the prevention gains by maintaining targeted respiratory outreach to assisted-living facilities and high-absenteeism schools until weekly indicators remain stable for four consecutive weeks. Move readiness from 88 to 90 by completing a full-scale shelter medical activation at the Civic Center with live patient-flow tracking, radio checks, and pharmacy dispensing simulation. Convert the biweekly corrective-action tracker into a standing dashboard reviewed at Public Health command staff meetings.

periods.analysis: By 2026-Q2, the communicable disease case rate fell from 38.1 to 31.2 per 100k, the strongest green result in the eight-quarter arc and a good population-health outcome for a growing coastal suburb. The Emergency Response Readiness Score improved from 88 to 89, again one point short of the >=90 target and therefore still yellow. The Civic Center functional exercise improved patient-flow timing and radio reliability, but the after-action review found that backup dispensing staff for the Bayview pharmacy pod were not fully cross-trained. We should recognize the progress without declaring victory: disease prevention is performing well, and readiness is close, but the last point matters in a real emergency.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the low case rate by continuing wastewater monitoring, urgent-care reporting, and summer camp illness protocols through the high-visitor season. Close the final readiness gap by cross-training Bayview pharmacy pod backups, validating the dispensing roster in a no-notice drill, and updating the emergency operations plan annex with lessons from the Civic Center exercise. If those items are completed before the next scoring window, Harborview should be positioned to move the Emergency Response Readiness Score to the >=90 target.

periods.analysis: June's communicable disease rate of 31.2 per 100,000 was below its ceiling, but September surveillance has not been verified here. The last readiness score, 89, remains short of 90, with Bayview pharmacy pod backup training still identified in the exercise follow-up. Current EPA lead-service-line guidance also makes coordination with drinking-water staff a prudent preparedness task; this is outside context, not evidence of a Harborview lead exposure event.
periods.recommendations: Verify the September surveillance extract and complete the backup-staff drill before rescoring readiness. Coordinate resident-facing water-service-line guidance with Public Works & Utilities so health and utility messages remain consistent, without asserting an exposure that has not been documented.
